experimental_protocol.measurement_condition: PBS rinse before every impedance measurement
experimental_protocol.edta: pH 7.4; fresh 25/25/50/50 mL for successive 15/15/30/30 min segments
experimental_protocol.urea: Saturated urea prepared with 75% ethanol, 20 mL, 10 min

layers.inner_table.initial_calcium_mol_p.source: Order-of-magnitude mineral-calcium prior based on bone-mineral composition, not rat measurement.

stages.acetic_acid.k_r_m3_per_mol_s.inne.source: Apparent H+ leaching constant for compact inner table; theoretical prior.

stages.edta.k_r_m3_per_mol_s.source: Aggregate legacy range kept for the frozen ensemble protocol; superseded by per-layer entries below. Apparent chelation constant at pH 7.4.

stages.edta.k_r_m3_per_mol_s.outer_table.source: Apparent EDTA chelation constant on SCM-exposed outer-table surfaces; theoretical prior.

stages.edta.k_r_m3_per_mol_s.diploe.source: Apparent EDTA chelation constant on pre-exposed diploe pore walls; theoretical prior.

stages.edta.k_r_m3_per_mol_s.inner_table.source: Apparent EDTA chelation constant on SCM-exposed inner-table surfaces; theoretical prior.

stages.edta.surface_site_capacity_mol_pe.source: Finite exchangeable surface-calcium pool (Tiselius HA chromatography site mechanism), assumed ~4-27% of bulk calcium; requires isotherm measurement.
Finite pre-exposed surface-site pool in porous diploe (Tiselius mechanism), ~3-30% of layer calcium; theoretical prior.
Finite exchangeable surface-calcium pool for inner table (Tiselius mechanism); theoretical prior.

electrical.archie_exponent.source: Empirical conductivity-porosity exponent for standardized post-rinse resistance estimates.

protocol_assumptions: Acetic acid is interpreted as 50% v/v, giving a nominal total concentration of 8.74 mol/L; apparent kinetics absorb non-ideal concentrated-solution effects.
The experimental sequence is 50% acetic acid (1 mL, 5 min), pH 7.4 EDTA in four fresh-bath segments (25/25/50/50 mL for 15/15/30/30 min), then saturated urea in 75% ethanol (20 mL, 10 min).
PBS rinsing before every impedance measurement is approximated as complete pore-liquid reset at stage and EDTA-segment boundaries; solid calcium and porosity are retained.
Urea is transported but does not consume mineral calcium in the baseline model; no irreversible urea-swelling or ethanol-tissue effect is activated.

The in-vitro boundary is stage-specific: 50% acetic acid contacts only the outer table (stages.acetic_acid.boundary_mode=outer_only, zero inner flux); EDTA and urea use complete centrifuge-tube immersion (boundary_mode=immersed), so both outer and inner table surfaces contact the same bath. For prospective in-vivo outer-table application, set the relevant stage to outer_only.
The electrical calculation is a standardized post-rinse series-resistance estimate, not a prediction of SSVEP SNR or PLV.

Acetic-acid dissolution follows the ore-acidification leaching analogy (H+ diffusion through the reacted layer competing with surface reaction; JMA-type fast-then-slow deceleration emerges from SCM product-layer resistance rather than from an empirical time exponent; uranium-ore rate constants on a days timescale are NOT transferred).

Neutral EDTA chelation is limited by a finite exchangeable surface-calcium site pool per layer (Tiselius HA chromatography mechanism); the rate decays linearly with pool depletion and stops at the capacity, while compact-table exposure remains gated by the SCM reaction front.
